'''Gyula Y. Katona''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈkɒtonɒ ˈɟulɒ|lang}}; born 4 December 1965) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] working in [[graph theory]] and [[combinatorics]]. He is a professor and head of the Department of Computer Science and Information Theory at the [[Budapest University of Technology and Economics]] (BME), and a [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. His research concerns [[Hamiltonian path|Hamiltonian cycles]] in graphs and [[hypergraph]]s, [[graph toughness]], [[Matching (graph theory)|factors]], and [[graph pebbling]].<ref name="resume">{{cite web |title=Resume of Gyula Y. Katona |url=http://www.cs.bme.hu/~kiskat/resume.html |publisher=Budapest University of Technology and Economics |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref> In 2026 he was awarded the Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Merit of Hungary]].<ref name="sandorpalota">{{cite web |title=Az augusztus 20-i állami ünnepség kitüntetettjei |url=https://www.sandorpalota.hu/hu/az-augusztus-20-i-allami-unnepseg-kituntetettjei |publisher=Sándor-palota – Köztársasági Elnöki Hivatal |date=2026-08-20 |language=hu |access-date=2026-08-20}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Katona was born in [[Budapest]] in 1965, the son of the mathematician [[Gyula O. H. Katona]].<ref name="oneletr">{{cite web |title=Katona Gyula Y. önéletrajza |url=http://www.cs.bme.hu/~kiskat/oneletr.html |language=hu |publisher=Budapest University of Technology and Economics |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref> He attended the [[Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium]] and studied mathematics at [[Eötvös Loránd University]] from 1986 to 1991. His diploma thesis, ''A Few Versions of the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem'', was supervised by [[László Lovász]] and [[András Recski]].<ref name="resume"/><ref name="oneletr"/> He continued as a doctoral student at the same university from 1991 to 1994, and in 1997 received the degree of [[Candidate of Sciences]] from the Hungarian Academy of Sciences for the dissertation ''Paths and Cycles in Graphs and Hypergraphs'', again under the supervision of Lovász and Recski.<ref name="resume"/><ref name="mta">{{cite web |title=Katona Gyula Y. |work=Köztestületi tagok |url=https://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok?PersonId=15807 |publisher=[[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] |language=hu |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=97549}}</ref> In 2024 he was awarded the degree of Doctor of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="resume"/><ref name="mta"/>

== Career ==
From 1994 to 1997 Katona was a research assistant professor in the combinatorics department of the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|Mathematical Institute of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], and from 1997 to 1999 he held a [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science|JSPS]] postdoctoral fellowship at [[Ibaraki University]] in Japan.<ref name="resume"/> He joined the Department of Computer Science and Information Theory at the Budapest University of Technology and Economics in 1997, became an associate professor in 2002, and has headed the department since 2011.<ref name="resume"/><ref name="mta"/> He was appointed full professor by the [[President of Hungary]] with effect from 1 September 2025.<ref>{{cite journal |title=A köztársasági elnök 211/2025. (IX. 1.) KE határozata egyetemi tanárok kinevezéséről |journal=[[Magyar Közlöny]] |issue=100 |year=2025 |url=https://magyarkozlony.hu/dokumentumok/001f1763482014dfdccb95ad35998318b9a6521f/letoltes |language=hu |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref> He was a visiting professor at [[Arizona State University]] in 2006–2007, and has taught in the [[Budapest Semesters in Mathematics]] programme since 2003 and at the [[Aquincum Institute of Technology]] since 2010.<ref name="resume"/>

Katona was managing editor of the Hungarian-language journal ''Matematikai Lapok'' from 1994 to 1997, and serves on the editorial boards of the ''AKCE International Journal of Graphs and Combinatorics'' and the ''[[International Journal of Computer Mathematics]]''.<ref name="resume"/><ref name="mta"/>

== Research ==
Katona's research lies at the interface of graph theory and the theory of algorithms. Much of his early work concerns [[Hamiltonian path|Hamiltonian cycles]] and their variants.<ref name="oneletr"/> With [[Henry Kierstead]] he introduced a notion of Hamiltonian chains in uniform hypergraphs, the objects now commonly called tight Hamiltonian cycles, and gave a Dirac-type sufficient condition for their existence. The question of the optimal minimum-degree threshold became known as the Katona–Kierstead conjecture and was later proved in asymptotic form by [[Vojtěch Rödl]], [[Andrzej Ruciński]] and [[Endre Szemerédi]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Katona |first1=Gyula Y. |last2=Kierstead |first2=H. A. |title=Hamiltonian chains in hypergraphs |journal=[[Journal of Graph Theory]] |volume=30 |issue=3 |year=1999 |pages=205–212 |doi=10.1002/(SICI)1097-0118(199903)30:3<205::AID-JGT5>3.0.CO;2-O|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rödl |first1=Vojtěch |last2=Ruciński |first2=Andrzej |last3=Szemerédi |first3=Endre |title=An approximate Dirac-type theorem for ''k''-uniform hypergraphs |journal=[[Combinatorica]] |volume=28 |issue=2 |year=2008 |pages=229–260 |doi=10.1007/s00493-008-2295-z}}</ref> His other work includes results on [[graph toughness]] and its edge and local variants, on [[Matching (graph theory)|factors]] of graphs, on Hamiltonian-saturated graphs and hypergraphs, and on [[graph pebbling]] and rubbling.<ref name="resume"/><ref>{{cite journal |last=Katona |first=Gyula Y. |title=Searching for ''f''-hamiltonian circuits |journal=[[Combinatorica]] |volume=12 |issue=2 |year=1992 |pages=241–245 |doi=10.1007/BF01204727}}</ref>

He is the coauthor of three textbooks: ''Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Algorithms'' (with András Recski, Technical University of Budapest, 1993), ''Introduction to Finite Mathematics'' (Eötvös Loránd University, 1993) and ''Introduction to Computer Science'' (Typotex, Budapest, 2002).<ref name="resume"/>

== Awards and honours ==
* Rényi Kató Memorial Prize of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] (1991)<ref name="resume"/><ref>{{cite web |title=A Rényi Kató-emlékdíj díjazottjai 1971-től napjainkig |url=https://www.bolyai.hu/files/Dijak_Renyi_Emlekdij_osszes_2022.pdf |publisher=[[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] |language=hu |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref>
* Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Merit of Hungary]], civil division (2026), for his research on hypergraphs and his role in the mathematical education of engineers<ref name="sandorpalota"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Átadták az augusztus 20-i állami kitüntetéseket – Itt a díjazottak névsora |url=https://www.portfolio.hu/gazdasag/20260820/atadtak-az-augusztus-20-i-allami-kitunteteseket-itt-a-dijazottak-nevsora-857426 |work=[[Portfolio.hu]] |date=2026-08-20 |language=hu |access-date=2026-08-22}}</ref>
